Cross-Benchmark Generalization in Long-Horizon Agents

paper.arxiv.2608.00181

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2608.00181v1. Explicit effort-floor training reward and absent no-floor counterfactual establish a cross-benchmark training study. Connected companion analysis is a distinct paper, not an independent replication or new family. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Toolathlon informed initial base-family/teacher choices and contributed reused MCP surfaces, although no external benchmark tasks/graders entered training according to the authors. Pretraining contamination cannot be audited, the no-effort-floor ablation was not run, and exploratory outcome-conditioned behavior patterns do not establish a causal transfer mechanism.

Permanent record ID: repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2608.00181.limitation

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • This is one combined SFT-then-RL experiment; the stages are not isolated, and no no-effort-floor ablation was run.
  • Toolathlon influenced the initial base-family/teacher choices and contributed reused MCP surfaces. External tasks and graders are excluded from post-training according to the authors; base pretraining cannot be audited.
  • Updated greedy results and accepted-paper snapshots have distinct provenance. Native four-sample diagnostics are not identified with standard unweighted any-of-four pass@4; one run, correlated benchmarks and unavailable paired units limit uncertainty claims.
  • Deterministic Python final-state criteria supply reward. Kimi K2.6 generated the selected 3,000 warmup trajectories, and the low-score effort floor is capped at 0.40.
  • Claude Opus 4.8 assisted root-cause reports, after which authors checked raw trajectories. Exploratory outcome-conditioned behavioral patterns and correlations do not establish a causal transfer mechanism.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The paper post-trains Qwen3.5-122B-A10B on 363 MCP tasks using a selected 3000-trajectory Kimi K2.6 supervised warmup followed by one-epoch RL. Deterministic criterion rewards are combined with a low-score effort floor capped at 0.40; evaluation uses native benchmark scores rather than this shaping reward.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

For the updated greedy software-engineering evaluations, Table 2 reports SWE-BenchPro 20.5→26.3% and Terminal-Bench 2 44.9→47.7% after the combined SFT+RL pipeline. The authors report descriptive point estimates from one training run and distinguish these from older four-sample diagnostics and retained tau2 results.
